title: OOM propagation & CNI send-queue backlog - oncall scrapbook
summary: During a sustained load test (synthetic traffic ramp), several worker nodes experienced repeated container OOM kills which coincided with rapid growth of the CNI send queue on those nodes. Symptoms: pod-level OOMs, high kubelet eviction events, and CNI plugin transmit-queue lengths growing until packets were dropped and higher request latencies resulted. This doc is an oncall scrapbook capturing timeline, immediate mitigations, root-cause hypotheses we exercised, and follow-ups for a more robust runbook.
incident_timeline:
2025-09-10 09:12 UTC - Alert: increased 95th p99 latency for inference-route /v1/generate; Pager fired.
2025-09-10 09:14 UTC - Observed spike in pod restarts on three workers (ip-10-0-14-xx, ip-10-0-21-xx, ip-10-0-23-xx).
2025-09-10 09:15 UTC - Oncall pulled node metrics: node_memory_MemAvailable trending down, oom_kill_count incrementing on containerd.
2025-09-10 09:18 UTC - Network team flagged CNI send-queue (calico_send_queue_len) climbing on same nodes; tx drops increasing on veth interfaces.
2025-09-10 09:22 UTC - Performed targeted cordon + drain of two worst nodes to protect control-plane and reduce noisy neighbors.
2025-09-10 09:28 UTC - Kubelet logs show frequent kubelet eviction decisions (memory.available threshold).
2025-09-10 09:35 UTC - Recovered baseline latency after drains and container image cache warming; alerts subdued by 09:42 UTC.
2025-09-10 09:45 UTC - Post-incident checks: no etcd latency anomalies; API server healthy.
2025-09-10 10:05 UTC - Postmortem brainstorming and action assignment begun.
observations:
- OOMs started inside inference containers (oom-killer logs point to processes serving model shards).
- Kubelet evictions triggered quickly after memory spiking; eviction thresholds configured conservatively on these instance types.
- calico_send_queue_len metric (custom exporter) shows send queues rising before OOMs in time series.
- Interface tx_dropped and TX queue len (ethtool -S) spiked concurrently; suggests packets queued in kernel while CNI attempted to transmit.
- No sustained etcd warnings or API server errors; control plane not root cause.
- Node-level swap is disabled (explicit), so kernel OOM is primary reclaim pathway.
- Worker instance family shows bursty CPU + memory pattern during synthetic load; nodes were close to memory capacity pre-test (no prewarming).
hypotheses_tested:
- Hypothesis A: Memory leak in model process -> reproduced by running the same load in staging: memory growth matches production; ruling in process memory as contributor.
- Hypothesis B: CNI stalls cause backpressure and processes block accumulating ephemeral buffers -> tested by dumping socket queues and reading calico agent logs; found repeated \"send failed\" with EAGAIN and long queuing.
- Hypothesis C: Kernel-level networking issue (driver bug) -> checked kernel logs, no driver oops but tx timeout counters rose. Not primary.
- Hypothesis D: Kubelet eviction settings too aggressive causing cascading restarts -> verified thresholds; eviction occurred after kernel OOMs rather than preventing them. Partial contributor.
immediate_mitigations:
- Cordon + drain two saturating nodes to offload work (kubectl cordon/drain with --ignore-daemonsets).
- Restarted calico-node pods on two nodes to clear stuck send-queues (kubectl delete pod calico-node on nodes).
- Temporarily scaled inference deployment replicas down by 25% to reduce memory pressure during the test.
- Increased pod memory requests in staging to force scheduler to place pods on larger instances for next run.
- Ensured kubelet eviction thresholds left at defaults while we evaluate long-term change (avoid flapping).
root_causes:
- Primary: Pod memory usage growth during synthetic ramp pushed nodes to kernel OOM path; absence of swap and conservative kubelet eviction timing meant kernel OOMs occurred before graceful kubelet eviction could stabilize pods.
- Secondary: CNI send-queue growth amplified resource pressure — when node transmit queues backed up, processes handling RPCs/ingress blocked and memory buffers accumulated.
- Tertiary: Test environment lacked prewarmed model caches and had high pod density on smaller shapes leading to fragile margin for memory spikes.
long_term_actions:
- A1 (owner: Ravi) - Update SRE runbook: add section \"CNI send-queue indicators\" with quick PromQL checks and ip route/ethtool commands. due: 2025-09-26.
- A2 (owner: Maya) - Introduce a canary test that warms model caches before ramping load; embed into perf harness. due: 2025-10-03.
- A3 (owner: Luca) - Evaluate kubelet eviction vs. oom_killer ordering on our kernels and consider more proactive eviction (or system reserved memory adjustments) on inference pools. due: 2025-10-10.
- A4 (owner: Networking) - Add monitoring alert for calico_send_queue_len > threshold for >2min. Also instrument TX backlog via node exporter. due: 2025-09-19.
- A5 (owner: Infra) - Re-evaluate instance sizing for inference pool and pre-bake base model artifacts into images for faster warmup. due: 2025-10-01.
metrics_and_logs:
PromQL snippets used:
- calico_send_queue_len{node=~"ip-10-0-.*"} > 0
- rate(container_memory_usage_bytes{pod=~"inference.*"}[1m])
- increase(node_oom_kills_total[15m])
- sum by(node) (kube_pod_container_resource_requests_memory_bytes) / machine_memory_bytes
Logs & commands run:
- journalctl -u kubelet -n 100 --no-pager
- dmesg | grep -i oom
- sudo ss -s; sudo ss -o state established
- sudo ethtool -S eth0 | grep tx
- calicoctl node status && calicoctl get felixconfigurations -o yaml
- kubectl describe pod <pod> --namespace prod-inference (OOM messages shown)
- conntrack -L | wc -l (verified not a conntrack exhaustion event)
runbook_deltas:
- Insert new watchpoints: calico_send_queue_len and node tx_dropped thresholds.
- Add a short checklist for oncall: 1) check calico queue, 2) check dmesg for oom-killer, 3) confirm etcd/API server health, 4) cordon/drain plan, 5) scale down noisy deployments.
- Add safe command snippets for draining with minimal disruption (kubectl drain flags).
uncertainties_and_next_questions:
- Why did the send-queue growth precede OOMs on timeline in some nodes but not others? Is there a subtle kernel scheduling interplay causing blocked threads to accumulate memory?
- Are we seeing any hints of packet requeues at the CNI level that amplify memory use inside calico/node? Need deeper calico internal metrics.
- Should we move to instance types with slightly higher memory headroom for inference pools, or change packing strategy? Cost tradeoffs to be evaluated.
- Could a different CNI (or Calico config tweak: reduce per-queue buffering) materially reduce backpressure?
notes_to_self:
- Keep a short reproducible script to drive the failing pattern in staging (link to perf harness below).
- handy commands during triage: kubectl get events --all-namespaces --sort-by='.lastTimestamp' | tail -n 200; for node in <list>; do ssh $node 'sudo dmesg | tail -n 200'; done
- When restarting calico-node, watch for ephemeral routing flaps; prefer rolling restarts one node at a time.
- Don't immediately change eviction thresholds in prod during an ongoing incident; prefer cordon/drain and scaling adjustments first.
